Meeting header:

[00:00] Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How's everyone?
[00:08] Aditi: Hi, Aditi here. Thanks, Samira. We—yeah we're ready to go, legal and procurement on the line.
[00:12] Sofia: Hi, Sofia, procurement. Marcus on my side is on IT.
[00:16] Marcus: Hey all.
[00:18] Samira: Great. Goal for today is to walk through the MSA and DPA redlines you sent, go over the SLA options, confirm pricing approval process, and agree next steps for onboarding. Sound right?
[00:27] Aditi: Yes. I'll jump in when we hit legal points. We attached redlines earlier; biggest concern is data residency and contractual KMS responsibilities.
[00:35] Diego: Okay, I'll cover the deployment options and the technical parts that tie to KMS and audit logs. To start, Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and Private — VPC/on-prem. For regulated workloads you often look at Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
[00:49] Marcus: On that, do you have an option to bring-your-own-key? That's a requirement for us—so keys never leave our control.
[00:56] Diego: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated we offer KMS integration patterns; in hosted we can support customer-managed keys through a KMS proxy in certain regions. There was a note that sometimes the docs call it K M S proxy—so apologies if our docs are inconsistent.
[01:12] Aditi: Good, we can work with that. On the DPA, the data flow diagrams were a bit unclear, especially around inference caching and logs retention. Who owns audit logs?
[01:22] Samira: Good question. By default Redwood retains audit logs for operations needed for support and billing; customers can opt into extended retention as part of an add-on, and in Private deployments logs remain in your VPC by default. Diego, would you like to add?
[01:35] Diego: Yeah, so there are two layers—request/response logs for debugging (we can mask sensitive fields) and platform audit logs. For Dedicated and Private, the audit logs can be routed to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch export; for hosted, we offer a 90-day audited retention unless you opt in to longer retention. There might be a line in the DPA where we can tighten that up.
[01:55] Aditi: We need explicit language in the DPA that puts control of PII data in customer control and that logs containing PII won't be stored outside the EU for our EMEA workloads.
[02:05] Diego: Understood. We can propose a data residency appendix that binds region-specific storage and processing. There's a small nuance where model weights are in the public model catalog but inference for your tenant is region-locked.
[02:18] Sofia: On pricing, procurement wants a clear path for committed capacity discounts and an estimate for peak throughput. We need numbers to show up in our procurement packet.
[02:26] Samira: For Dedicated we have monthly commit tiers with predictable throughput—I'll pull the pricing sheet and include burst credits. Diego, we'll need to provide examples for typical tokens per second for a 2x and 4x concurrency profile.
[02:38] Diego: Yep, I can produce a small benchmark table for expected rps/latency per config; I'll note the sequencing and KV cache behavior which dramatically affects costs. For example, prefix caching reduces tokens by 20–40% for reuse patterns.
[02:50] Marcus: Sorry—K V cache? Is that the same as key-value cache?
[02:54] Diego: Right, sorry—KV cache, key-value cache, sometimes our slides say K V cash—typo. It's the mechanism we use to persist decoding state to speed up subsequent requests.
[03:04] Aditi: Another legal point: liability caps. Our standard vendor contract has a higher cap than what's in your MSA. Can Redwood accept the standard cap or at least scale with ARR?
[03:14] Samira: We typically have an ARR-based liability cap and for enterprise customers we can negotiate upwards. If you send a clause, we can review—our GC team often asks for a short turnaround.
[03:24] Aditi: We'll send the exact language. Also need SOC 2 Type II report and encryption whitepaper attached.
[03:30] Samira: We'll provide SOC 2 Type II and our security pack; Diego will attach a technical notes pack including KMS integration, key rotation, and audit log flows.
[03:38] Diego: I'll include diagrams showing VPC peering, traffic flow, and where keys are stored for Private/Dedicated options.
[03:44] Sofia: About the SLA—what are the uptime numbers and credits? Procurement's asking what remediation looks like for P1 incidents.
[03:51] Samira: We offer tiered SLAs—99.5% for hosted with limited credits, and 99.9% for Dedicated with stronger credits and SRE response targets. For Private deployments you can negotiate an enterprise SLA. Diego, want to give sample response times?
[04:02] Diego: For Dedicated, P1 response is within 1 hour and P1 mitigation engagement within 4 hours; for hosted it’s 4 hours response. We'll put exact times in the appendix. Credits are pro-rata service-day credits; we can show examples in the SLA appendix.
[04:18] Marcus: We need a clear escalation path; email isn't sufficient. Can you commit to PagerDuty integration and named SRE contacts?
[04:25] Samira: Yes, Dedicated customers get a named SRE contact and on-call escalation; PagerDuty integration is supported. We'll put that into the SLA appendix as well.
[04:34] Aditi: One more legal item: data deletion on termination—how quickly do you purge customer data and what proof can you provide?
[04:41] Diego: By default we have a 30-day retention on terminated tenants to allow for recovery, but for regulated customers we offer expedited purge with certificate of deletion within 7 days if included in the DPA. We'll add a clause to the DPA that allows a shorter purge window if required.
[04:56] Sofia: Great. Back to approvals—what's the internal timeline? Procurement needs to know when pricing and SLA language is final so we can route for sign-off.
[05:03] Samira: Ideally we circulate redlines and the SLA appendix this week; if you review by next Monday (2026-03-22) we can target contract execution the following week and onboard the week of 2026-03-30. Does that align?
[05:13] Marcus: That timeline works for IT to allocate resources for VPC peering and firewall rules.
[05:18] Aditi: Legal will try to get initial comments by 2026-03-19; procurement will need final pricing to route approval.
[05:24] Samira: I'll prioritize the MSA/DPA redline send and Diego will prioritize the SLA appendix and technical diagrams.
[05:29] Aditi: Also confirm whether there are export control or restricted model lists—are any models disallowed for certain geos?
[05:36] Diego: There are model catalog entries with region availability; we'll call out any models with restrictions and recommend vetted models for EMEA workloads.
[05:43] Sofia: Onboarding: what does the onboarding week look like—do you do a kickoff, integration tasks, runbooks?
[05:50] Samira: Yes—kickoff, SSO setup, network setup (VPC peering or transit), sample integration, and a golden runbook for ops. We'll share an onboarding checklist with dates and owners.
[05:59] Marcus: We'll need a staging window to run benchmarks before full cutover. Can we schedule that during onboarding?
[06:04] Diego: Absolutely. We'll run a bench with the same dataset and traffic profile you expect; we'll also include warm-up for KV cache to get realistic numbers.
[06:12] Aditi: A minor point: the MSA references 'Redwood Private' but in our redlines we used 'Redwood Privet' as a typo on our side—ignore that.
[06:19] (laughs)
[06:20] Samira: Noted.
[06:22] Sofia: Are there any contractual dependencies on third-party sub-processors we should watch for?
[06:27] Samira: We list sub-processors in the DPA appendix; for Private deployments there's minimal third-party exposure, but for hosted we use cloud providers for compute. We can include a sub-processor list and a 30-day notice for changes.
[06:38] Aditi: Perfect. Anything else from your side?
[06:42] Diego: I'll add a short note about performance degradation modes and automatic fallback to smaller models—helps with graceful degradation if capacity is constrained.
[06:50] Marcus: That seems reasonable. We prefer to avoid silent quality regressions, so that behavior should be explicit.
[06:56] Samira: Okay, summary of action items—Samira sends redlined MSA/DPA, Diego sends SLA appendix and technical pack, Aditi will return legal comments, Sofia will gather procurement packet details and preferred PO flow.
[07:09] Aditi: Correct. Expect our initial legal comments by 2026-03-19.
[07:13] Sofia: Procurement will try to finalize pricing approval by 2026-03-22.
[07:17] Samira: Great — we'll follow up with the documents today. Thanks everyone for your time.
[07:22] Marcus: Thanks.
[07:24] Diego: Thanks all.
[07:26] Samira: Bye.

End of meeting.
